text: Guide: Insurance Litigation (TRG), Ch. 7A. [3:326 - 3:334] Reserved. 2. [3:335] Wrongful Termination Claims: Coverage for wrongful termination claims under CGL policies depends on the type of claim asserted. Most wrongful termination claims combine both contract and tort theories. [See B & E Convalescent Ctr. v. State Comp. Ins. Fund (1992) 8 CA4th 78, 85, 9 CR2d 894, 898, fn. 5; and ¶ 3:506 (contract claims)] [3:336 - 3:354] Reserved. a. [3:355] No “bodily injury liability” coverage: Tort claims raised in connection with employment termination are generally not covered under CGL “bodily injury” coverage for the following reasons: (1) [3:356] Often no “bodily injury”: First, most employment termination claims seek damages for nonphysical injuries (emotional distress, mental anguish, etc.). Most cases hold that claims for emotional distress, unaccompanied by physical injury, do not constitute “bodily injury” and thus are not covered: “The term ‘bodily injury’ is unambiguous.
